lines.text: The IRS may call your unpaid family loan a gift.
lines.say: The IRS may call your unpaid family loan a gift.

lines.text: It happens a lot: 32% of people who lent to a friend weren't repaid last time (LendingTree, July 2025).
lines.say: It happens a lot. In a July twenty twenty-five LendingTree survey, thirty-two percent of friend lenders weren't repaid last time.

lines.text: So the IRS asks: was it a loan, or a gift?
lines.say: So the IRS asks: was it a loan, or a gift?

lines.text: Forgive it, and it's a gift. In 2026, gifts over $19,000 to one person need a gift tax return, usually with no tax due.
lines.say: Forgive it, and it's a gift. In twenty twenty-six, over nineteen thousand dollars to one person needs a gift tax return.

lines.text: A real loan gone totally worthless is a short-term capital loss, with proof you tried to collect.
lines.say: A real loan gone totally worthless is a short-term capital loss, with proof you tried to collect.

lines.text: Example: $5,000 bad debt, 22% bracket, no gains. Only $3,000 a year offsets income: $660 saved, then $440.
lines.say: Example: a five thousand dollar bad debt, twenty-two percent bracket, no gains. Only three thousand a year offsets income, so six hundred sixty saved, then four hundred forty.

lines.text: Interest-free family loans over $10,000 can trigger imputed interest.
lines.say: Interest-free family loans over ten thousand dollars can trigger imputed interest.

lines.text: Paperwork helps prove it: a signed note, a payment schedule, and collection attempts.
lines.say: Paperwork helps prove it: a signed note, a payment schedule, and collection attempts.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: The IRS might treat your unpaid family loan as a gift
post.ig:
The IRS may call your unpaid family loan a gift.
32% of people who lent a friend money didn't get it back last time (LendingTree, July 2025).
Forgive a loan and it's a gift: over $19,000 to one person in 2026 means a gift tax return (usually no tax due).
A real loan gone totally worthless is a short-term capital loss, offsetting capital gains, then up to $3,000 of other income a year.
Hypothetical: $5,000 bad debt, 22% bracket, no other gains, saves $660, then $440 the next year.
Sources: IRS Topic 453, IRS Topic 409, IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, LendingTree.
